title: 2025 AMC 10B Problem 20
statement:
Four congruent semicircles are inscribed in a square of side length \(1\) so that their diameters are on the sides of the square, one endpoint of each diameter is at a vertex of the square, and adjacent semicircles are tangent to each other. A small circle centered at the center of the square is tangent to each of the four semicircles, as shown below.

The diameter of the small circle can be written as \((\sqrt{a} + b)(\sqrt{c} + d),\) where \(a,\) \(b,\) \(c,\) and \(d\) are integers. What is \(a + b + c + d?\)

solutions.text: Let each semicircle have radius \(\rho,\) with centers like \((\rho, 0)\) and \((1, \rho).\) Adjacent semicircles are tangent, so these centers are \(2\rho\) apart: \((1 - \rho)^2 + \rho^2 = 4\rho^2.\) This gives \(2\rho^2 + 2\rho - 1 = 0,\) so \(\rho = \tfrac{\sqrt3 - 1}{2}.\) The small circle of radius \(t\) sits at \(\left(\tfrac12, \tfrac12\right),\) and it’s tangent to a semicircle when its distance to that center equals \(\rho + t.\) That distance is \(\sqrt{2 - \sqrt3},\) so \(t = \sqrt{2 - \sqrt3} - \rho,\) and the diameter is \(2t = \sqrt6 - \sqrt2\) \(- \sqrt3 + 1 = (\sqrt3 - 1)(\sqrt2 - 1).\) So \(a + b + c + d = 3\) \(+ (-1) + 2 + (-1) = 3.\) Therefore, the answer is A.
hints: First find the semicircle radius \(\rho\) from the tangency of two adjacent semicircles whose diameters start at neighboring vertices
The small radius equals (distance from the square’s center to a semicircle’s center) minus \(\rho;\) then factor \(2t\) into two binomials
